items.title: New US rules change how international students can stay in America
items.description: WASHINGTON: A major change in the US immigration system is set to take effect on Tuesday, requiring international students to keep closer track of how long they are authorised to remain in the country. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is ending the longstanding “duration of status” system for F-1 students and replacing it with a fixed period of admission. Under the new rule, F-1 students will generally be admitted for the length of the academic programme listed on their Form I-20, up to four years, with a 30-day period to arrive before the programme begins and 30 days to prepare for departure after the programme or authorised post-completion training ends. Students who need additional time to complete their current programme, begin a new programme, or undertake post-completion OPT or STEM OPT will have to take additional steps. They may apply to US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) for an extension of stay, or leave the United States and seek a new period of admission from Customs and Border Protection when they return. DHS advises students to work with their college’s designated school official before applying for an extension. Students seeking an extension must file Form I-539 with USCIS after receiving the appropriate recommendation on an updated Form I-20. What happens to students already in America? The change does not mean that every F-1 student currently in the United States has to file a new application on Tuesday. Students who are in the United States in F-1 status under the existing duration of status system on September 15 may remain without applying for an extension until the applicable programme or OPT/STEM OPT end date, subject to the transition rules. For these students, the transition period generally runs no later than November 14, 2030. There is an important exception involving travel. Current F-1 students who leave the United States after Sept 15 may be readmitted under the new fixed-period system, rather than continuing under duration of status system. Students who are considering international travel should therefore speak with their designated school official before leaving the country. New rules for students’ academic plans The rule also imposes new restrictions on changes during an F-1 student’s academic career. Among other changes, undergraduate students generally cannot change their educational level or major during the first year of a program without an exception for extenuating circumstances. Graduate-level students face additional restrictions on changing educational levels, majors and transferring schools. The rule also reduces the departure period after completion of a program or post-completion OPT/STEM OPT from the previous 60 days to 30 days for students subject to the new system. New immigration forms The Sept 15 change also affects USCIS paperwork. Students filing Form I-539, used to request an extension or change of nonimmigrant status, or Form I-765, used to apply for employment authorisation, should use the new editions required by USCIS beginning Tuesday. Students should check the edition date before filing because USCIS will not provide a grace period for use of the previous editions. For international students, the most important point is that Sept. 15 is not a blanket deadline to leave America or file a new application. It marks the beginning of a new system in which admission is tied to a specific period, and students who need additional time may have to obtain an extension or a new period of admission. Universities urge students to check travel, immigration records Major US universities are advising international students to pay particular attention to travel plans and their Form I-94 as the new rules take effect. Harvard University, Yale University, Columbia University, Cornell University and Stanford University have issued guidance explaining the changes and urging students to consult their international offices before making immigration or travel decisions. Yale says students already in the United States under the old “duration of status” system generally do not need to take immediate action on Sept 15. But students who travel abroad and return after that date will generally receive a new I-94 with a specific “admit until” date. Yale advises students to check the I-94 after every international trip. Harvard similarly warns that international travel after Sept 15 can affect future OPT and extension-of-stay planning. Its international office advises students to understand the consequences before making travel plans. Columbia and Cornell have also published detailed guidance on the transition rules, while Stanford has warned that F-1 and J-1 students will no longer be admitted under the D/S notation after the rule takes effect. The message from the universities is essentially the same: students should not assume that Sept 15 itself requires them to leave or file a new application, but they should understand their individual I-94, program end date, OPT plans and the consequences of international travel. The Department of Homeland Security is also ending the “duration of status” system for J-1 exchange visitors and certain I-visa holders, including representatives of foreign information media. They too will generally be admitted for a fixed period rather than indefinitely for the duration of their program or assignment. J-1 participants who need additional time will generally have to seek an extension of stay, while the rules for I representatives are tied to the length of their media assignment. The change does not apply broadly to other major nonimmigrant categories such as H-1B, L-1, O-1 or B-1/B-2 visas, which already operate under fixed periods of admission.

items.title: FIA arrests TLP regional emir in terror financing case
items.description: LAHORE: In a major breakthrough, the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has arrested Syed Inayatul Haq Shah, the North Punjab emir of banned Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP), on the multiple charges, including terror financing for the violent march of the party in October 2025 . The FIA has also obtained the nine-day remand of the accused. A senior official told Dawn the suspect was one of the eight key financiers of the TLP arrested by a joint team of the counter terrorism wing (CTW) of the FIA from Lahore, Islamabad and Rawalpindi. He said the raid was carried out by tracking down the location of Shah in Rawalpindi. During the inquiry, the official said, the CTW of the FIA traced 1,800 suspected accounts reportedly used by Inayatul Haq Shah, his family members and other suspects to finance the banned party. “We have arrested the key figure of the TLP, Syed Inayatul Haq Shah, in the case registered against him with the police station of the counter terrorism circle Lahore,” said the FIA official. He added that an inquiry established that Shah, along with his accomplices, had withdrawn Rs13.4m cash from a madressah’s account on Oct 13 and 14, 2025 when the TLP’s violent march was taken out from Lahore and it reached Muridke. The FIA official said that such huge withdrawals had given a reasonable cause to suspect that said amount was used for financing the violent March. “During the inquiry, the financial profiling and counter-terrorism-financing analysis of leadership, financiers, associates and related persons of the TLP was conducted, particularly with reference to financial transactions having relevance to the violent TLP mobilization/Muridke incident,” reads the FIR, a copy available with Dawn . The FIR pointed out Oct 9 to 15, 2025 when the transactions were made. During scrutiny of bank statements, the FIA’s CTW Lahore stated that details, institutional accounts and other available record of Syed Inayatul Haq Shah alias Sultanpuri and his father Syed Ziaul Haq Shah surfaced due to substantial financial activity through personal and associated religious/madressah accounts immediately before and during the violent protest period. During the inquiry, a considerable time was provided to Syed Inayatul Haq Shah and Syed Ziaul Haq Shah, requiring them to join the enquiry and explain the huge cash withdrawals and movement of funds amounting to Rs13.4m, including the source, purpose, authority and utilisation; however, they failed to appear and join the enquiry proceedings. Published in Dawn, September 15th, 2026

items.title: O/A Level papers leak likely originated abroad, NA committee told
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A parliamentary committee was informed on Monday that the leakage of O/A level papers had originated likely from some other country as no evidence was found to establish its link with Pakistan. The National Assembly Standing Committee on Federal Education and Professional Training, which met with acting Chairman Anjum Aqeel Khan in the chair, besides other agenda items discussed the papers leakage issue of O/A level exams. The committee was informed that the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), after examining the matter, “found no evidence to establish that the leakage had originated from Pakistan.” The committee was further informed that NCCIA does not have direct access to servers located abroad, which limits its ability to independently trace the source, location and mechanism of any alleged leakage occurring through overseas servers. Lawmakers express concern over growing menace of narcotics in educational institutions In May this year, the government had ordered a probe into the alleged leakage of Cambridge examination papers, directing NCCIA to investigate in coordination with Cambridge Assessment International Education (CAIE) amid concerns raised by parents and students over the alleged leakage of some papers. Meanwhile, the committee expressed grave concern over the growing menace of narcotics in educational institutions and observed that the increasing reports of drug use and supply to students required immediate, coordinated and result-oriented action by the concerned authorities. The committee stressed the need for an effective coordination mechanism among the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF), police, Higher Education Commission (HEC) and Federal Directorate of Education (FDE) to identify the sources of drug supply and prevent the involvement of criminal elements in and around educational institutions. The committee said the responsibility for ensuring a safe, secure and drug-free learning environment requires a coordinated response involving educational institutions, law-enforcement agencies and regulatory authorities with clear responsibilities, effective monitoring and strict enforcement. The committee sought verified data on reported cases of drug use and supply in educational institutions, including the number and nature of cases, action taken by the concerned authorities, the mechanism adopted for inter-agency coordination and details of the penalties and punishments awarded to those found involved. The committee observed that mere establishment of committees and formulation of policies would not be sufficient unless accompanied by effective implementation, regular monitoring and visible action against those responsible for supplying narcotics to students. The meeting was informed that Anti-Drug and Tobacco Committees had been established in higher educational institutions to monitor and address issues relating to drug and tobacco use among students. The members, however, stressed that such institutional mechanisms must be strengthened and linked with law-enforcement and regulatory authorities to ensure timely reporting, investigation and action in cases involving narcotics. Meanwhile, the committee stressed the need to make the programmes of National Vocational and Technical Training Commission (NAVTTC) more outcome-oriented and aligned with international labour market requirements. The meeting observed that the global employment landscape was changing rapidly, particularly in the Middle East, and emphasised the importance of continuously assessing emerging demand for skilled manpower in international markets. Similarly, Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (FBISE) informed the meeting that pursuant to the recommendations of the subcommittee, a number of measures had been introduced to facilitate students with dyslexia during examinations. These measures included provision of additional time and assistance in reading the question paper to students requiring such support. The committee stressed the need for regular psychological support and the availability of trained remedial teachers in educational institutions to identify learning difficulties at an early stage and provide appropriate assistance to affected students in the classroom. A member stated that legislation relating to dyslexia had also been enacted by the Punjab Assembly, highlighting the need for a comprehensive and uniform approach to address the educational needs of children with dyslexia. The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) informed the committee that it would take up the matter with all boards to promote uniform measures and ensure that appropriate facilities and support mechanisms for students with dyslexia were adopted nationwide. Published in Dawn, September 15th, 2026

items.title: Madhubala faces life-threatening medical emergency
items.description: A crane belt supports Madhubala so she can stand and make small movements.—Dawn KARACHI: Safari elephant Madhubala fighting multiple illnesses for over a year now faces a life-threatening medical emergency as she’s unable to stand up on her own, it emerged on Monday. Sources said the female elephant suddenly “collapsed” on the ground on Monday morning, forcing the Safari authorities to arrange a crane to lift her up. “Our team is supporting her with a crane’s belt to keep her standing and make small movements. At the same time, we are constantly in touch with Sri Lankan wildlife health specialist Dr Budhika Bhandara over her condition,” Safari Park Director Amjad Zaidi told Dawn . He added that Madhubala had developed swelling on her right hind thigh that’s apparently preventing her from using her leg. Safari Park official says the elephant has developed swelling on right hind thigh that is preventing her from using her leg “The swelling could be the result of a fight with her companion Malika. A conclusive thing, however, could only be said once all tests including an X-ray and blood and urine tests are done, which will be carried out by our local team of experts,” he said. About Madhubala’s illnesses, Mr Zaidi said that she had recovered well from tuberculosis after undergoing an 18-month treatment course as well as a foot infection. “She is eating now and seems fine, otherwise,” Mr Zaidi claimed. However, the sources described Madhubala’s condition as life-threatening. “Madhubala is too weak now. If she fails to recover soon, her disability will seriously affect other organs of her body and may cause her death,” a senior vet feared. Madhubala had been in solitary confinement at Karachi Zoo following the tragic death of her companion Noor Jehan who died in 2023 after a tragic fall in her enclosure. Noor Jehan’s autopsy report released by the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) showed that she died from a severe blood parasitic infection and internal trauma combined with a lack of proper medical care. Left alone at the zoo, Madhubala was successfully relocated to Safari Park where she was reunited with her sisters , Sonia and Malika, in November 2024, under the supervision of Four Paws — an international animal welfare organisation that worked extensively with the KMC for elephant care. The success story of her reunion faded soon as Sonia died a month later after collapsing in her Safari enclosure. Lab reports later showed that she suffered from multiple chronic illnesses, affecting almost all vital organs, indicating prolonged neglect in her care and failure in timely diagnosis. Successive deaths of captive elephants raised public outcry, forcing the KMC to set up an 18-member body to look after Madhubala and Malika, both of whom were diagnosed with tuberculosis. The four female elephants were brought to Karachi from Tanzania in 2010 at a very young age under a controversial arrangement. Published in Dawn, September 15th, 2026

items.title: Business community split over SBP move
items.description: LAHORE/ISLAMABAD: The business community on Monday gave a mixed response to the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) decision to keep the policy rate unchanged at 11.5 per cent, with some backing the move while others called for further cuts to revive investment and industrial activity. The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) has expressed disappointment over the decision of the SBP’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to maintain the policy rate at 11.5pc, saying trade and industry are in dire need of some breathing space amid the current stagnation-prone economic environment. The apex trade body has termed the decision as highly contractionary and counterproductive — warning that holding the benchmark interest rate at an oppressive level will continue to severely stifle economic activity and undermine industrial revival efforts across the country. “Monetary policy was the only, but potent, tool available to the authorities to provide some relief at the moment, but it remained unutilised,” it added. FPCCI President Atif Ikram Sheikh said the business community had demanded a reduction in the policy rate to single-digit to help bring down the exorbitant cost of doing business. He elaborated that the central bank’s overly cautious approach directly contradicts current economic realities — and, denying much needed support to trade & industry as trade deficit has climbed by 18.1pc in July-August 2026 on year-on-year basis. He maintained that the industry is currently battling an existential crisis driven by elevated energy tariffs, burgeoning petroleum prices, geo-economic uncertainty, and sky-high financing costs, direc­tly resulting in stagnating industrialisation across the country. The Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OICCI) termed the SBP’s decision to keep the policy rate unchanged at 11.5pc a prudent and balanced approach in the current economic environment. It said that while inflation and core inflation remained elevated, stronger foreign exchange reserves, robust remittances and an uneven industrial recovery supported the case for avoiding further tightening at this stage. The decision provides businesses with policy continuity and some space for investment planning; however, the pause should not be seen as a substitute for reforms, the OICCI said. The chamber urged the government to reinforce monetary stability through fiscal discipline, energy-cost rationalisation, tax predictability, expedited tax refunds and faster ease-of-doing-business reforms so that macroeconomic stability could translate into stronger competitiveness, investment and sustainable private-sector-led growth. The Rawalpindi Chamber of Com­merce and Industry supported the MPC’s decision to maintain the policy rate at 11.5pc, saying global inflationary pressures arising from the conflict in the Middle East involving Iran had pushed up international energy and commodity prices. As a net importer of fuel, Pakistan remains directly exposed to these shocks. “In such an environment, a steady hand on monetary policy protects the stability that has been achieved with considerable effort over the past two years,” RCCI President Usman Shaukat said in a statement issued on Monday. The Korangi Association of Trade and Industry President Muhammad Ikram Rajput expressed that high interest rates were slowing the recovery of industrial activity, new investment and the export sector. Published in Dawn, September 15th, 2026

items.title: Civil society decries delay in hearing Imaan, Hadi’s pleas
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Veteran journalists and members of civil society have expressed profound concern over the continued delay in deciding the applications filed by human rights lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha, seeking suspension of their sentences pending appeal. Despite the Supreme Court’s explicit direction of May 12, 2026, ordering the Islamabad High Court to decide the matter within two weeks, the applications remain unresolved. The repeated adjournments, amid the continued incarceration of the two prominent rights defenders, have raised serious concerns about the accessibility of timely and effective judicial remedies in the country. The veteran journalists and civil society members who have expres­sed concern over the delays include Hussain Naqi, Farhatullah Babar, Zahid Hussain, Mustansar Javaid, Anwar Iqbal, Ali Ahmad Khan, Maz­­har Abbas, Dr Nazir Mahmood, Dr Touseef Ahmed Khan, Nasir Zaidi, Asmatullah Niazi, Munizae Jahangir, Mahnaz Rahman, Sohail Sangi, Nasir Malick, Adnan Reh­­mat, Iqbal Khattak, G.N. Mughal, Waris Raza, Habib Khan Ghori, Fouzia Shahid, Lala, Ayub Jan Sar­handi, Shafiq Awan, Abdul Sattar, Mohammed Riaz, Ayub Malik, Fauzia Rana and Jamil Ahmed. While the substantive merits of any legal application remain strictly within the purview of the courts, prolonged procedural delays can raise serious questions regarding fundamental constitutional guarantees. The ongoing delay, they said, undermines protections relating to liberty, due process and fair trial as enshrined in Articles 4, 9 and 10-A of the Constitution. The signatories are particularly concerned about the wider chilling effect that prolonged legal proceedings and incarceration pending appeal may have on the legal fraternity and independent human rights defenders. The state and the administration of justice must ensure that individuals engaged in lawful, rights-based advocacy are not subjected to judicial processes that effectively become punitive in themselves, they said. The journalists and civil society members emphasised that the rule of law is strengthened not merely by the formal existence of legal remedies, but by ensuring that such remedies remain accessible, timely and effective. With the next hearing scheduled for September 17, they urged the Supreme Court to ensure that the suspension applications are heard and decided without further delay, in order to uphold the sanctity of constitutional guarantees and the principle of timely justice. Published in Dawn, September 15th, 2026

items.title: Govt increases petrol by Rs4.42 per litre, HSD by Rs6.10 per litre amid rising global oil prices
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday increased the price of petrol by Rs4.42 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.10 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs380.24 per litre while HSD will cost Rs409.42 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 15 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: US judge blocks new stay limits for foreign students, journalists
items.description: A US federal judge on Monday blocked a Trump administration rule that would impose fixed limits on how long foreign students, exchange visitors and representatives of foreign media may stay in the United States. Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV of the District of Massachusetts granted the plaintiffs' request to postpone the rule's effective date under Section 705 of the Administrative Procedure Act. The rule was scheduled to take effect on Tuesday. The new rule, published by the US Department of Homeland Security in July, would have replaced the "duration of status" system currently applied to F-class academic students, J-class exchange visitors and I-class representatives of foreign information media with fixed periods of admission. Under the rule, F and J non-immigrants would generally be admitted for the duration of their academic or exchange programs, subject to a maximum of four years, followed by a 30-day departure period. Those needing additional time to complete their studies, training or exchange programs would need to apply to US Citizenship and Immigration Services for an extension. I-class foreign media representatives would be admitted for the period necessary to complete their activities or assignments, for no more than 240 days at a time, with extensions available. Several organizations, including NAFSA: Association of International Educators, the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, the American Federation of Teachers, the United Auto Workers Local 2322, the NewsGuild-CWA and others, filed a lawsuit on August 18 seeking to block the rule.

items.description: Alors que la République démocratique du Congo en pleine guerre, subit de plein fouet un retour dévastateur d’Ebola sous la forme d’une nouvelle souche, le Bundibugyo, déclarée en mai 2026 et qui a déjà fait au moins 3300 morts pour plus de 6 800 cas recensés, le président Félix Tshisekedi, lui, s’est invité sur d’autres fronts. Une nouvelle constitution qui pourrait bien lui ouvrir la voie d’un troisième mandat et l’organisation d’un dialogue national, donc en principe inclusif, constituent les nouvelles priorités du chef de l’Etat congolais. Mais, dans sa volonté officiellement affichée de recherche de la paix dans son pays, le président de la RD Congo ne va-t-il pas plutôt vers un effritement total de la cohésion nationale? Sauf que cette interrogation ne se pose absolument pas pour le président de la république qui vient de profiter de la paisible journée dominicale du 13 septembre 2026, pour signer l’ordonnance créant le comité en charge des préparatifs de ce raout national. Certes, les dates de ce qui pourrait n’être qu’un leurre de plus, dans la quête de la paix, ne sont pas encore fixées, mais le dialogue sera contenu, en principe, dans une période de trois mois. Si dans une patrie écartelée par des querelles intestines, toute initiative née dans le but d’amener ses enfants à se parler est louable, et même noble, il n’en demeure pas moins que l’action doit être guidée par l’objectivité, et surtout la sincérité. Ce qui n’est visiblement pas le cas pour l’instant, au vu des premiers pas de l’instance en préparation. Au lieu d’un arbre à palabre sous lequel toutes les parties auront leur mot à dire afin de crever l’abcès pour de bon, et provoquer une catharsis, le risque est grand que la rencontre se transforme en un gigantesque banquet auquel prendront part des convives qui acclameront des décisions qui seront aussitôt rejetées par les vrais acteurs qui eux, risquent d’être écartés par un pouvoir expert en diversion. Comme le résument et le dénoncent déjà les principaux partis de l’opposition, et certaines organisations de la société civile, Félix Tshisekedi qui détient tous les rouages de l’organisation placée sous son contrôle, ne sera, ni plus, ni moins que juge et partie. En tout cas, si tant est, que le président de la république aspire réellement à la cohésion nationale et croit encore à la démocratie, dans l’intérêt de populations prises entre les feux nourris, au propre comme au figuré, de l’AFC/M23 et l’appétit boulimique d’Ebola, il doit abandonner son projet de 3e mandat qui est à la base de toutes ses manœuvres politiques actuelles. Et il est encore temps pour lui de sortir de son obstination suicidaire de règne sans partage. Il n’est jamais tard pour bien faire, surtout que l’architecture du dialogue n’a pas encore une forme définitive. En dehors de la durée, ni les noms du président, ni ceux des participants, encore moins les dates d’ouverture et de clôture du fameux dialogue, ne sont connus. Questions: qui, mieux que tous les opposants politiques de Felix Tshisekedi, eux qui sont les véritables protagonistes de la vie politique, et l’AFC/M23, ennemi juré des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) dans le Kivu, ont leur place autour de la table des débats? Félix Tshisekedi se rappelle-t-il encore qu’il est opposant, et surtout fils du célèbre opposant Etienne Tshisekedi, pour qui l’alternance constitutionnelle constituait l’essence du combat politique? En tout cas, Felix Tshisekedi, en bon gentleman, peut encore sortir des rails de son monologue exclusif pour emprunter les voies d’un véritable dialogue inclusif, gage d’un retour de la paix durable en RD Congo. Par Wakat Séra L’article RDC: Felix Tshisekedi prépare son monologue exclusif! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: ‘The Flood is the Point’
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Donald Trump loves a deal, even if, at times, it’s just the idea of a deal. The president’s trade dispute with Canada continues to drive one of America’s closest allies into a closer relationship with its chief competition. Although Trump is insisting that “Canada wants to make a deal very badly,” there is very little evidence that’s true, as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney—enjoying broad national approval for his combative response to the American leader—looks to strengthen its alliances in Europe and Asia. Meanwhile, AI leaders are publicly calling for a slowdown. That was the gist of the message delivered by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei this weekend in an essay warning that the technological advances of AI are outpacing the ability to ensure that they are safe. His concerns were echoed by some of the biggest names in tech—OpenAI leader Sam Altman and Elon Musk. But the president saw something else in their warnings: “There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China,” Trump wrote on his social-media site this morning. This week on Radio Atlantic , my colleagues Ashley Parker and Tom Nichols join me to discuss the president’s trade war with Canada, the Trump-centric Republican midterm convention in Dallas, and whether an aging Congress can regulate AI. The following is a transcript of the episode: Ashley Parker: To be somewhat fair to Trump, or to anyone, is that this is just fundamentally incredibly complex. If you’ve ever watched these members of Congress—which is basically a gerontocracy—try to get to the bottom of Snapchat or Instagram or social media with teens, right, it’s like they’re speaking a foreign language, and those are table stakes, right? AI is a million times more complicated than posting a problematic video on YouTube or Instagram. Adam Harris: This is Radio Atlantic . I’m Adam Harris. Congress is back on Capitol Hill for the last time before the midterm elections, and they have a lot to think about—the burgeoning trade war with Canada and warnings from tech CEOs about the dangers of unregulated AI, among other things. And when those lawmakers return to the campaign trail for the final stretch, the ones in competitive districts may have some company—members of the president’s Cabinet. With me to discuss the news of the week are my colleagues Ashley Parker and Tom Nichols. Let’s get to questions. Welcome to the show. Parker: Thanks for having us. Tom Nichols: Thanks, Adam. Harris: Ashley, I want to start with you because you had a story that ran recently about something that people I think have become a little bit desensitized to, and that’s the potential violations of the Hatch Act, which limits the partisan political activities of federal employees. You and our colleague Michael Scherer reported on a competition among the Cabinet secretaries to travel to competitive electoral districts. Can you sort of walk us through that reporting? Parker: Sure. So the first way we heard about this competition, which was not public, was almost inadvertently. We were speaking with a Cabinet secretary who said that there was an event in New York that they had kind of wanted to attend, but had declined because they didn’t want to get docked points in the competition. And we were immediately like, What competition? And so it turns out that there is this unofficial travel competition in the Trump White House. It’s overseen by a woman named Meghan Bauer, who basically coordinates with all of the Cabinet secretaries, officially running between Memorial Day and Labor Day. And basically the goal is to encourage Cabinet officials, Cabinet secretaries to travel the country, particularly to swing districts or swing states that are competitive in the midterms. And each time they go to one of these areas, they get a point. And what this Cabinet official was worried about was losing points, although the official was mistaken. When we began reporting, many officials at the White House told us, Nobody ever loses points; you only accrue points . And they even said, Look, if someone is heading to New York to, say, do a hit on CNN, to talk about Trump’s policies, that still would count as a point . Harris: We can talk about it in point systems, but we should also think of it in terms of the law, right? Like, is this a Hatch Act violation? Parker: So, no, not inherently, but it brings Cabinet officials potentially quite close to the line, and it’s something they need to be careful of. So just to put it in a little historical perspective, this general thing of wanting your top officials, your Cabinet officials, out in the country selling the president’s policies, especially in the run-up to a midterm election, is incredibly common. [George W.] Bush did it; [Barack] Obama did it; [Joe] Biden did it. And Biden, I remember, the most in-demand Cabinet official at the time, when he was president in the run-up to the midterms, was Pete Buttigieg. So Cabinet officials can go and they can talk about—especially if it’s related to their jobs, an agriculture secretary, for instance, or let’s just take Pete Buttigieg for an example. Pete Buttigieg could travel the country and talk about how this stimulus package that Biden and Democrats helped to pass had brought a bridge to your district, had brought new roads to your state, was responsible for huge construction projects over here that had created jobs. That’s all totally fine and not a Hatch Act violation. If it becomes more overtly political—showing up in a district at a campaign stop with, say, a Senate candidate and just saying, Hey, vote for Ken Paxton in Texas —that is where you get into problems. And the Trump officials, some of them have gotten into problems. Harris: Tom, how do you process the sort of flood, the stream of controversy, that comes from the administration? Nichols: Well, I actually am intimately familiar with the Hatch Act because people filed complaints against me constantly when I was a federal employee, before I came to The Atlantic . I was a professor at the Naval War College, which meant I was a Defense Department employee, but I wrote articles and I wrote op-eds and I spoke my mind. And I always finish with, These are my personal views, speaking as an American citizen, et cetera, et cetera . So I think Ashley’s description of, boy, right up to the line, is a great way to think of it. And the larger point, I think, is that, Adam, like you asked: Why does this happen? How do we cope with this flood? And I think that the flood is the point. The fire hose is the point, because at some point, you just sort of throw up your hands and say, Which of these, you know, 9 million things? It used to be that, even in the first Trump term, somebody getting hit with a Hatch Act violation was a big deal. I mean, it made the news. Kellyanne Conway, there were couple of other— Parker: Yeah, I remember the Kellyanne Conway one. And it stood out, right? Nichols: Yeah, right. Because it was rare. And because it was so obvious. And I think it’s part of that whole fire-hosing strategy, where you just sit back and say, Okay, fine. I give up, because tomorrow there will be something else . And then the Hatch Act will seem relatively minor by comparison. Parker: I was thinking about this as I was biking into work today, which is, if you even just look at today’s news, Hatch Act violations are comparatively quaint, right? I mean, I’m biking in, I see that ProPublica has reported that a Russian oligarch who’s very close to [Russian President Vladimir] Putin bankrolled Donald Trump Jr.’s intimate wedding a few months ago. And amid all these warnings that AI is going to kill us in a doomsday scenario, President Trump came out and said, We’re not slowing down; there’s no regulations . So if a Cabinet official says, Hey, vote for this Republican congressman , in the panoply of things that watchdog groups are worrying about, it’s not top of the list, to be frank. Nichols: I know the broken-windows theory of crime has been more or less discredited, but there is a kind of feeling of this of, It starts with the Hatch Act . The Hatch Act is like turnstile jumping in the subway, but enough people do it enough times and pretty soon, you know, it’s people shooting at each other in the streets and robbing banks. And it kind of feels that way now. There are no guardrails. I mean, the story that Ashley just mentioned, about Don Jr.’s wedding. Again, if you were a federal employee, if you even talked to a Russian, that was paperwork right there. I could not imagine saying, Oh yeah, and by the way, he paid for my wedding . But we’ve just kind of gotten used to it. Harris: Republicans gathered in Dallas, Texas, last week for a sort of unusual midterm convention. What did we learn about where Republicans are right now, if anything, coming out of that convention? Nichols: We learned that the party belongs to Donald Trump and that thousands of people will repeat every word he says if he tells them to. That, I think, tells you everything you need to know—about the party, not about the election, but about the party. Parker: I think that’s about right, because a lot of Republicans did not think this was a good use of time or money. If you’re actually focused on winning the midterms, they wanted to be campaigning in their districts, in their states—let alone for some of them, depending on the district or the state, aligning themselves with a president who’s quite unpopular and whose policies are quite unpopular. But nonetheless, you still saw a number of them travel to Dallas despite not really wanting to, because as Tom said, Trump is the leader of this party and he demanded a midterm convention, so he got one. Harris: I was, as I was watching it go on, thinking about what was driving the news as we were heading into the convention, which was this sort of burgeoning trade war with Canada. Trump himself mentioned Canada briefly during the convention, saying— Donald Trump: Canada very much wants to make a deal. They’re dying to make a deal. Harris: Tom, that’s all well and good, but the reality is that the president has chosen to squabble with one of America’s closest allies. Where do things stand now between the U.S. and Canada? And is there any sense of a thawing? Or do you think things are continuing to heat up? Nichols: Well, first, let’s always point out that the president’s default response to any controversy is that Country X is desperate to make a deal . It’s literally Donald Trump’s Mad Lib—one of the Mad Lib sentences. You know, What do you think about the controversy with Country X? The answer is always, Controversy will be over soon. Country X is begging to make a deal. They’re calling me every day , whether it’s Canada, Iran, the Houthis, you name it. I think the Canadians have simply decided they’ve had enough of this nonsense. They are no longer partners; they are adversaries in the economic space. But I think that the Canadians have said, Fine . A majority of the Canadians don’t want to pay for this Trump–Carney tariff war, but they support Carney standing up to Trump. And so my guess is this is not retrievable until Trump is gone from office, which is a real tragedy, even if Trump backs down from the tariffs, which he almost certainly is going to do sooner rather than later, I think. Harris: Yeah. And as you mentioned, right, Carney’s approval rating is quite high. Ashley, how has he been responding to the president, and how has the back-and-forth been going in recent days? Parker: Well, I sort of understand Carney in his response going back to a speech he gave much earlier this year at Davos, where he basically said, The world order as we— I’m paraphrasing here— the world order as we know it is over. And all of these sort of smaller countries have always supplicated themselves to the United States for protection or for deals or for various reasons, and that’s no longer a good strategy for us . And so I think Carney’s response in this trade war is him sort of acting on those principles he laid out at Davos. And one thing that was so striking to me when you look at the back-and-forth—and it looks like both sides had issues; it’s hard to point specifically to which side blew up the most recent deal—but one thing that comes through is Trump has talked about wanting Canada to be a 51st state, and that mainly seems to be trolling, except not entirely; there’s always a kernel of truth with everything Trump does. But in these negotiations, it feels like the American side has sort of internalized the idea that Canada is less a sovereign nation and more a 51st state. And when you look at the terms that Canada objected to, it was stuff the United States negotiators demanded, which would be reasonable if Canada was a state, but is not reasonable if Canada is a sovereign nation and an ally to our north. And it feels like that’s where things fell apart. Harris: Tom, actually in your piece the other day, you talked about the way that the president doesn’t view other nations as sovereign nations. There’s just this idea that he can’t go in and extract things in the way that he would if it were just a part of something that he already owned. Can you sort of flesh out that idea a little bit? Nichols: Well, I mean, not to psychoanalyze the president from a distance, but I think most people would agree the president’s a pretty narcissistic guy. He’s got to put his name on everything. He builds monuments to himself. Every sentence begins with I . And people like that don’t think of other people as real people; they think of them as players on the stage that surrounds them. And I think that’s very clear with Donald Trump. This convention, going back to the convention we were mentioning, you know, he doesn’t really think of other people trying to win elections, and he doesn’t care. They’re supposed to come to his big party and wear a hat and bring noisemakers and that’s it. And that’s the extent of his interest. And I think that’s how he is with foreign countries, that he says they’re all kind of wholly or partially owned subsidiaries of Donald Trump Incorporated . He doesn’t think of them as real places with unique cultures or particular interests led by human beings who may not actually see the world the way he does or care about his interests as much as he cares about his interests. And that’s partly why you always get these kind of stock answers of They’re gonna make a deal, because of course everybody makes a deal, because that’s what I want. And they’re gonna do what I tell them to do, because of course, all my life, everyone has done what I tell them to do . It flummoxes him completely when a foreign nation says, We’re not going to do that . And one of the reasons—you know, I don’t want to extend this analogy by Canada too far—but I think that’s one of the reasons he’s having such a hard time with the war of choice he began in Iran. He just can’t imagine that—he says, I demand that you do X, Y, and Z . And the Iranians say, No and here’s a bunch of missiles and drones as part of that answer . And I think he totally unravels him, because he’s just never had to deal with that. And I think when Mark Carney, you know, as Ashley was saying, Who is this uppity governor, to speak to the president in this way? , instead of the leader of a sovereign nation and place that’s part of NATO and has real interests in the world—one of our second or third biggest trading partners. He cannot internalize that. It doesn’t make it—it’s not like he rejects the idea. It’s like he can’t grasp the idea. Parker: And just to briefly follow on Tom, I mean, Trump has such legitimate faith and confidence in himself as a dealmaker that he really can’t fathom that. You may recall that when he was campaigning, he said, On day one, the war between Russia and Ukraine will end , which is a sort of promise presidents make— day one signals it’s a priority. But in talking to Trump’s aides, they’re like, No, no; he actually thought that . Like, he actually thought that he was such a good dealmaker, it would end. And obviously it hasn’t. Harris: When we come back, we talk about the danger of AI, and Ashley and Tom talk about what they’ll be reporting on in the week ahead. [ Music ] Harris: I wanna switch gears a little bit, speaking of the idea of things that people can and cannot control. Over the last several days, CEOs of leading AI companies have been sounding the alarm, really in a lot of the same ways that Bill Gates, when he was on the show with Hanna [Rosin] not that long ago, was talking about the growing risks of artificial intelligence and the products and the ways that people are using those products. Trump doesn’t appear to be heeding those concerns and has responded that the U.S. has to, quote, “ win AI. ” What is your reaction to this, to all of this? Nichols: That’s a classic Trump answer. You know, We have to win AI . That’s the president’s way of saying, I didn’t understand the question. I don’t really know what this is, and so we just have to win it. Because that’s a good kind of standard. You could have filled in anything: What do you think about the, you know, international chocolate-milk market? Well, we have to win that. Parker: Yeah, is winning AI , we die first? Nichols: Yeah. ( Laughs. ) What does that mean? Parker: I will confess, I don’t fully understand all of the intricacies of AI either, but from what I do understand, to be somewhat fair to Trump, or to anyone, is that this is just fundamentally incredibly complex. And, you know, lawmakers, one problem you have is if you’ve ever watched these members of Congress—which is basically a gerontocracy—try to get to the bottom of Snapchat or Instagram or social media with teens, right, it’s like they’re speaking a foreign language. And those are table stakes, right? AI is a million times more complicated than posting a problematic video on YouTube or Instagram. So first of all, a lot of the people in the United States responsible for possibly regulating this are like me, which is terrifying—can’t begin to possibly understand the nuances or the complexities. And the second thing is, even if the United States is willing to regulate, the question is you would sort of need a mutually-assured-destruction pact with China and with other countries. This is a sort of globalized problem. Nichols: I understand the intricacies very well because I have seen all the Terminator movies. And I know that Skynet is going to become self-aware at some point, and we’re going to regret it. But to go back to the president’s response, that would have been a more reassuring answer. So that’s a highly complex thing. We want to make sure that we’re handling it responsibly. And I’m fascinated to know what happened that spooked all of the top, you know, that spooked Altman and Musk and all these other guys. But I’m less of a doomer about it—even if it does scare me. But I think that the first wave of damage, if something like this gets loose, will be economic. But I still don’t know. And, you know, to go back to where we were, I don’t know what it means to win that, other than to say that we will use it to capture more efficiencies than other countries will and put more people out of work faster or something. But I think the danger of this thing is real because the people handling it—I just don’t have a sense that they are looking at this with the kind of civic responsibility that they should have. Harris: Ashley and Tom, I’m going to ask you to open your notebooks. What questions do you have going into this week? And, Ashley, I’m going to go to you first. Parker: Sure. So I’m gonna be looking at—I think actually last time I was on your podcast, we were talking about the midterms and why the bottom hasn’t fallen out for the Republicans yet. And, you know, that that was August, but things really kick off after Labor Day. There’s October surprises; voters tune in. I mean, one thing that was fascinating is I talked to someone who does focus groups with swing-state voters who said, You hold up a picture of the Senate candidate in a state, and half the voters don’t even know who he or she is . So I’m still gonna be asking those similar midterm questions, but at a time when everyone is tuning in and ads land harder; mistakes, gaffs land harder; trying to see where this heads in November. Harris: And the Republicans are starting to put more of their money into their advertising now. They’re sort of using that war chest we were talking about the last time. Parker: Yeah, because again, part of this is: They would have liked to have used it earlier. Trump has a lot of money; his groups have a lot of money. But he had to kind of release it. And even if they didn’t spend it, they wanted to get those TV reservations up early because you can get a cheaper rate if you book early. But the other reason you spend now is because this is when people are paying attention. And Michael Scherer and I spoke to Trump’s pollster Tony Fabrizio, who said at the time when we spoke, he said, Look, yeah, things are bad for the Republicans, but that’s because we haven’t turned to the Democrats yet . The Democrats have a horrible brand, and you should expect to see a ton of contrast ads because elections, as Biden always says, and as everyone understands, They’re a choice . Nichols: Ashley mentioned, or Adam, I think you mentioned October surprises. And I’m looking for one because when Trump—it gets panicky. I think one of the things I saw at the convention was that he felt very ebullient and energized, but also there was a lot of fear there. He clearly is deeply worried. And when he gets like that, you’re gonna get a surprise of some kind. He’s gonna. And it’s making me wonder what kind of thing will pop. So I guess I’m worried politically about a black-swan event, where he just does something to change the discussion. The other thing I’m watching, though, is that both in Russia and Iran, these situations are not going away. They are aware that there’s an election impending. And I have to say I don’t know why this is, but late September, early October is always a very fertile time for an international crisis. And I’m concerned that that crisis could erupt either in the Pacific, in Russia, or in Iran, because they’re not on our timetable. They’re not gonna do things on Donald Trump’s timetable or do things based on his interests. And I think all of those places that we’ve stopped watching temporarily because of so much going on at home are percolating, and I’m concerned about what happens next in each of those three, especially in the Ukraine war and in Iran. Harris: Well, Ashley, Tom, thank you so much for joining me today and helping me sift through the news of the week. Parker: Thank you for having us. Nichols: Thanks, Adam. Harris: That’s all for today’s show. This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Mike Pesoli and edited by Hadley Robinson. It has original music by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. If you like what you saw here, new episodes of Radio Atlantic drop every Monday and Thursday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube page, on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work and the work of my colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Until next time, I’m Adam Harris.

items.title: Modernisation de l’Administration : cap sur des services publics plus efficaces et proches du Peuple
items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a présidé, ce lundi 14 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la session ordinaire du Conseil national de la modernisation de l’Administration et de la bonne gouvernance (CN-MABG). Les travaux ont permis d’évaluer les performances de l’Administration publique, d’identifier les insuffisances persistantes et de définir les orientations pour l’année 2027. À l’ouverture de la session, le Chef du Gouvernement a rappelé que la modernisation de l’Administration publique constitue un enjeu de souveraineté, de dignité et d’efficacité de l’action publique. Elle ne saurait, selon lui, se limiter à des réformes techniques ou à la dématérialisation des procédures. « Notre ambition doit être claire : faire de l’Administration publique un véritable instrument de souveraineté et de transformation du Burkina Faso », a-t-il déclaré. Le Premier ministre a ainsi appelé à un changement profond des pratiques, des méthodes de travail et du rapport de l’Administration au Peuple. L’objectif est de bâtir une Administration disciplinée, intègre, compétente, performante, innovante et redevable, capable de produire des résultats et de rendre compte de l’utilisation des ressources publiques. La performance globale de l’Administration au titre de l’année 2025, établie à 85,38 %, témoigne, selon le Chef du Gouvernement, d’une dynamique appréciable. Tout en félicitant les agents publics ayant contribué à ce résultat, il les a invités à se garder de toute autosatisfaction. « La performance n’est pas une fin en soi : elle est une exigence permanente », a-t-il souligné, insistant sur la nécessité de traduire les résultats administratifs en améliorations concrètes dans la vie des populations. Les travaux ont également permis d’examiner les principales insuffisances qui affectent encore le fonctionnement de l’Administration. Elles concernent notamment la faible couverture de l’évaluation de certaines institutions, l’appropriation insuffisante des outils de gouvernance, les contraintes liées aux ressources humaines et aux infrastructures, les difficultés des systèmes d’information ainsi que l’authenticité de certains documents produits dans le cadre de la commande publique. L’appropriation des plateformes de services numériques par les citoyens figure également parmi les défis identifiés. À ce sujet, le Premier ministre a appelé à une transformation numérique inclusive, adaptée aux réalités nationales et qui ne crée pas de nouvelles formes d’exclusion. Il a notamment souhaité que les langues nationales trouvent progressivement leur place dans les systèmes d’information et les services numériques. Au cours de la session, les participants ont examiné trois principaux documents : le rapport annuel de mise en œuvre de la Stratégie nationale de modernisation de l’Administration publique, le rapport sur l’état de la gouvernance au Burkina Faso et le rapport global sur la performance des structures de l’Administration publique, tous au titre de l’année 2025. Ils ont également analysé les résultats des évaluations des stratégies nationales relatives à la déconcentration administrative, à la modernisation de l’Administration publique et à la promotion de la bonne gouvernance. À la clôture des travaux, le Premier ministre a engagé les responsables concernés à transformer les recommandations adoptées en actions concrètes, assorties de responsabilités clairement définies et de mécanismes rigoureux de suivi. Il a précisé que les insuffisances relevées ne remettent pas en cause les performances enregistrées, mais constituent des défis prioritaires auxquels des réponses doivent être apportées. Les orientations définies pour 2027 devront notamment permettre à l’Administration d’accompagner la reconquête du territoire et le retour effectif de l’État auprès des populations. « Là où nos Forces combattantes reconquièrent des espaces, notre Administration doit être prête à rétablir durablement la présence et l’autorité de l’État », a affirmé le Chef du Gouvernement. Pour Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, le rétablissement de la sécurité doit s’accompagner du retour de services publics adaptés aux besoins des populations, notamment dans les domaines de l’éducation, de la santé, de l’état civil, de la justice, de l’action sociale et de l’administration territoriale. Le Premier ministre a enfin appelé chaque ministère, institution, structure et agent public à prendre sa part dans la refondation de l’Administration, sous le sceau de la primauté de l’intérêt général. Il a chargé le ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, à travers le Secrétariat permanent de la modernisation de l’Administration et de la bonne gouvernance, d’assurer un suivi rigoureux de la mise en œuvre des conclusions et orientations issues de la session. items.title: Droits d’auteur au Burkina Faso : Plus de 2 milliards de FCFA mis en paiement par le BBDA pour la session d’août 2026
items.description: Réuni en conférence de presse le lundi 14 septembre 2026, le Bureau Burkinabè du Droit d’Auteur (BBDA) a présenté les résultats et les modalités de paiement relatifs à la répartition des droits du mois d’août 2026. Portée par un montant net de 1 522 424 728 FCFA, en progression de 11,61 % par rapport à l'année précédente, cette opération intègre également 550 745 105 FCFA au titre des droits en instance. Au total, plus de 2 milliards de FCFA seront versés dès ce mardi 15 septembre 2026 à 32 852 bénéficiaires, témoignant de l'engagement de l'institution en faveur de la transparence et de la valorisation du travail des créateurs. Le Bureau Burkinabè du Droit d’Auteur (BBDA) a animé une conférence de presse le lundi 14 septembre 2026 afin de faire le point sur l'opération de répartition des droits du mois d’août 2026. Dans sa déclaration liminaire, le Directeur Général du BBDA, le Camarade Zita Daniel BONZI, a souligné que cette rencontre s'inscrit dans une démarche continue de transparence et de dialogue avec les titulaires de droits et le grand public. Pour cette session, les redevances globales collectées s’élèvent à 2 395 288 544 FCFA. Après déduction des retenues statutaires, le montant net mis en répartition s’établit à 1 522 424 728 FCFA, contre 1 364 040 522 FCFA en août 2025, soit une hausse remarquable de 11,61 %. Plus de 32 000 bénéficiaires et résorption des droits en instance À cette somme nette s’ajoute une enveloppe de 550 745 105 FCFA correspondant aux droits en instance issus des exercices 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 ainsi que des sessions de février et mai 2026. L'ensemble de ces ressources porte le montant total mis en paiement à 2 027 361 636 FCFA au profit de 32 852 bénéficiaires, dont 16 346 membres affiliés au BBDA. Ces derniers perçoivent à eux seuls 1 412 867 131 FCFA, soit environ 93 % des droits nets répartis. De plus, le BBDA octroie un Droit Minimum Payable (DMP) de 3 900 FCFA aux membres concernés, ce qui représente une dotation globale de 63 749 400 FCFA. Catégories de droits et précisions sur la répartition individuelle Au cours de la rencontre, la Camarade Delphine SOMÉ/ZONGO, Directrice de la Documentation Générale et de la Répartition, a explicité les bases techniques régissant les calculs. La répartition du mois d’août englobe plusieurs catégories : les Droits de Reproduction Mécanique (provenant des éditeurs de phonogrammes et vidéogrammes), les Droits de Reproduction par Reprographie (dont une part revient à la presse écrite), la Rémunération Équitable au titre des droits voisins, la Rémunération pour Copie Privée et les droits collectés à l’étranger. Toutefois, le Directeur Général a rappelé que la hausse de la masse globale répartie ne garantit pas automatiquement une augmentation des gains individuels, chaque part dépendant directement du degré d'exploitation effective des œuvres. Démarrage effectif des paiements et canaux de règlement Le lancement officiel des règlements est fixé au mardi 15 septembre 2026. Afin d'assurer un processus fluide et sécurisé, le BBDA diversifie ses modes de paiement : virements bancaires, règlements par paiement mobile ( mobile money ), chèques pour les sommes égales ou supérieures à 100 000 FCFA, et paiements en espèces disponibles aux guichets de Ouagadougou et de Bobo-Dioulasso. L’article Droits d’auteur au Burkina Faso : Plus de 2 milliards de FCFA mis en paiement par le BBDA pour la session d’août 2026 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Nouna : une soirée d’horreur au secteur 4, deux morts et un homme maîtrisé après une série d’agressions.
items.description: Un marchand de bétail aurait tué son épouse et son ami, incendié des engins et semé la panique jusque dans une mosquée. Un dozo, intervenu avec courage, aurait contribué à éviter un bilan plus lourd. Une tragédie d’une rare violence a frappé le secteur 4 de Nouna dans la soirée du dimanche 13 septembre 2026. Selon plusieurs témoignages recueillis, un homme identifié comme Soré Sayouba, âgé de plus de 40 ans, polygame et père de six enfants, aurait commis une série d’actes meurtriers avant d’être maîtrisé par un brave dozo. Originaire de Dara et marchand de bétail, l’intéressé aurait d’abord agressé sa troisième épouse, Afousétou Soré, étudiante et future élève infirmière. Âgée de 26 ans, mariée et mère d’une fillette de quatre ans, Afousétou est étudiante à l’Université Nazi Boni de Dédougou, où elle a validé sa deuxième année en économie et mathématiques avec une moyenne de 14/20. D’après les témoignages, il l’aurait poursuivie avant de l’atteindre à son domicile et de l’égorger sur son lit. Un ami attiré sur les lieux, puis tué. Selon les témoignages recueillis, Daouda Zallé a alors été agressé à son tour. Il aurait été poignardé à plusieurs reprises, puis son corps a été jeté dans le feu des engins incendiés. Un autre ami, nommé Souley, a également été appelé par le mis en cause. À son arrivée, il aurait découvert ce dernier armé d’une machette et d’une daba. « Il m’a dit qu’il avait tué sa femme. Il tenait une machette et une daba avant de se jeter sur moi. Je me suis sauvé dans un champ de maïs », a-t-il témoigné tout en se lâchant avec une voix nouée » C'est une grande chance pour moi ». Le courage d’un dozo pour éviter un bilan plus lourd C’est dans ce contexte qu’un dozo présenté comme Kassoum Dama, originaire du village de Sanso, serait intervenu. Il aurait réussi à maîtriser et à ligoter le mis en cause. Selon son témoignage, l’homme lui aurait alors demandé de l’achever. « Lorsque j’ai pu le ligoter, il m’a dit de le terminer pour de bon. » Toujours selon ce témoignage, le mis en cause aurait évoqué, dans un discours jugé incohérent, un projet visant à éliminer quatre personnes avant de se donner lui-même la mort. L’intervention de Kassoum Dama aurait ainsi permis de mettre fin à la série d’agressions et, potentiellement, d’éviter d’autres victimes. Une tentative de suicide après les faits Après ces événements, Soré Sayouba aurait tenté de se suicider en se blessant avec sa machette et sa pioche. Il aurait subi des blessures à la gorge et à la tête. Des proches rapportent qu’il aurait récemment répudié sa troisième épouse, allant jusqu’à incendier ses effets personnels. Ils affirment toutefois n’avoir constaté aucun signe manifeste de démence avant le drame : l’homme fréquentait ses amis et échangeait normalement avec son entourage. Un autre témoignage, recueilli au cimetière municipal, évoque un possible traumatisme ancien. Selon un jeune homme présent sur les lieux, l’intéressé aurait échappé, il y a longtemps, à une attaque terroriste le jour du marché hebdomadaire de Bomborokuy où il a été pour l'achat du bétail, un événement qui lui aurait causé un choc psychologique. Il aurait eu du mal à retrouver son domicile à Nouna après l'attaque. Ce récit, qui n’a pas été confirmé par une source médicale ou officielle, ne permet pas, à lui seul, d’établir un lien avec les actes commis dimanche. Une ville sous le choc Ce lundi 14 septembre 2026, l’émotion était vive à la morgue, au cimetière municipal et dans les différentes familles des victimes. La douleur des proches se mêlait à l’incompréhension face à une violence aussi soudaine. Au-delà de l’horreur des faits, ce drame soulève de nombreuses interrogations sur les circonstances ayant conduit à cette explosion de violence. Seule une enquête rigoureuse, appuyée au besoin par une expertise médicale et psychologique, permettra d’établir les faits, les responsabilités et les éventuels facteurs explicatifs. En attendant le mis en cause a été arrêté et transmis aux forces de sécurité. Aux dernières nouvelles ,il a subi des soins intensifs au CMA de Nouna et son pronostic vital n'est pas engagé. Quant aux deux victimes, elles ont été inhumées dans la matinée du lundi au cimetière municipal de Nouna. Source: Madi Sidparaadye Kébré Burkinaweb. net L’article Nouna : une soirée d’horreur au secteur 4, deux morts et un homme maîtrisé après une série d’agressions. est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Contrôles de prix des produits de grande consommation : la BMCRF maintient la pression
items.description: L a Brigade Mobile de Contrôle Économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) poursuit sa mission de contrôle des prix des produits de grande consommation dans la capitale et ses environs. Les équipes de contrôle ont inspecté boutiques et supermarchés et petits détaillants de rue afin de vérifier le respect des prix fixés par les autorités. Plusieurs points de vente ont été sommés de modifier immédiatement les prix affichés, jugés non conformes à la réglementation. Les contrevenants devront s’expliquer devant la BMCRF et s’acquitter des amendes prévues par les textes en vigueur. Au cours des opérations, des produits périmés et de contrefaçon ont également été retirés du marché, renforçant ainsi la protection des consommateurs contre les pratiques frauduleuses. 80 00 11 84/80 00 11 85/80 00 11 86 BMCRF, la garantie d’une concurrence saine et loyale. items.title: Production de données statistiques : le Burkina 1er en Open data en Afrique de l’Ouest
items.description: L’Institut national de la statistique et de la démographie a tenu sa première session ordinaire du conseil national de la statistique de l’année, le 11 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, sur le thème : « Les statistiques publiques au service de la mise en œuvre du suivi-évaluation et de la redevabilité du Plan de relance 2026-2030 ». L’Institut national de la statistique et de la démographie (INSD) veut renforcer le rôle des statistiques publiques dans la conduite des politiques de développement. C’est dans cette perspective que s’est tenue le vendredi 11 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la première session ordinaire de l’année du Conseil national de la statistique (CNS). Placée sur le thème : « Les statistiques publiques au service de la mise en œuvre du suivi-évaluation et de la redevabilité du Plan de relance 2026-2030 », la rencontre a réuni des représentants des ministères, ainsi que les différents acteurs du système statistique national. Cette première session ordinaire de l’année a permis d’examiner le rapport statistique national 2025 et de valider le projet de Programme statistique national 2027. La rencontre a été l’occasion de mettre en avant la volonté du Burkina Faso de disposer de données produites et maitrisées au niveau national. Le président du CNS est le ministre de l’Economie et des Finances. Il a été représenté à cette session par le Secrétaire général (SG) du département Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama. Selon lui, dans la mise en œuvre du 5e Schéma directeur de la statistique (SDS)2026-2030 dont le coût global est estimé à 96,689 milliards F CFA, l’enjeu est de parvenir à un système statistique moderne, performant et fiable. L’activité statistique en progression malgré les défis Il a présenté cette orientation comme un choix de souveraineté, permettant au pays de produire lui-même les informations nécessaires à la compréhension de ses réalités et à l’orientation de ses politiques publiques. Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama a souligné que malgré un contexte sécuritaire difficile, les activités statistiques ont enregistré une progression en 2025. « Le taux d’exécution est passé de 65,6 % en 2024 à 67,8 % en 2025 », a-t-il révélé. Un projet de Programme statistique 2027 évalué à 10,6 milliards F CFA Cette performance, a poursuivi le SG du ministère en charge de l’économie, s’accompagne également d’une reconnaissance internationale dans le domaine de l’open data. En effet, le Burkina Faso s’est classé premier en Afrique de l’Ouest et deuxième à l’échelle du continent dans le classement mondial de l’open data, avec un score de 77 points sur 100, a-t-il indiqué. « Ces résultats reflètent un engagement collectif dont je remercie l’ensemble des acteurs du système statistique national », a-t-il clamé. Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama a invité l’ensemble des acteurs à maintenir leurs efforts, poursuivre l’innovation dans la production et l’utilisation des données, et faire des statistiques un véritable outil d’aide à la décision et un levier du développement durable. Face à l’évolution des besoins en matière d’information statistique, l’INSD entend également s’appuyer sur les nouvelles technologies pour moderniser ses méthodes de travail. Le directeur général de l’INSD, Toubou Ripama, a énuméré quelques innovations. Il s’agit de la création de l’observatoire national d’innovation statistique, du déploiement d’un centre d’appel dédié aux enquêtes par téléphone, de la prise en compte de l’intelligence artificielle, de la digitalisation des outils de collecte, ainsi que de la modernisation des plateformes de diffusion des donnés. Pour Toubou Ripama, ces différentes actions traduisent la volonté de l’INSD de construire un système statistique davantage adapté aux réalités et aux besoins futurs du Burkina. Le projet de Programme statistique national 2027, soumis à l’examen du CNS, est évalué à 10,6 milliards F CFA. L’Etat burkinabè va prendre en charge 52,7 % du financement selon le directeur général de l’INSD. « Cela traduit l’appropriation nationale croissante de notre système, tout en rappelant la nécessité de poursuivre la mobilisation des ressources pérennes et de partenariats diversifiés », a-t-il indiqué. Galedie Kétoura SIMPORE Issouf SANKARA (Stagiaire) L’article Production de données statistiques : le Burkina 1er en Open data en Afrique de l’Ouest est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .
